title: POC weekly sync - throughput optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput numbers from internal perf run, tune continuous batching and concurrency targets, and agree next steps to run expanded benchmark with queueing rules and autoscale tweaks. Discussed observed tail latency with bursts, KV cache hit rates, and tradeoffs between larger batches and per-request latency. Agreed to run controlled test with 12 concurrency / queue depth 100 and to share updated benchmark spreadsheet and a short how-to doc for config changes.
next_steps: Redwood to run 3 controlled benchmarks with proposed concurrency/queue settings and share CSV (Alex)
MapleHealth to confirm SLAs and whether tail-latency > 300ms is acceptable for web-facing flows (Sofia)
SE to send short config how-to for continuous batching + KV cache hints (Priya)
Schedule deep-dive on security/PKI if MapleHealth decides private deployment (Marta to coordinate)
Share benchmark spreadsheet link and update after runs (Alex)
action_items: Priya Nair: send continuous-batching config how-to + KV cache tips (due 2026-03-12)
Sofia Park: validate acceptable tail latency for product flows and confirm by 2026-03-14
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're on for the POC weekly throughput sync. quick roll call?
[00:06] Sofia Park: Sofia here, hi.
[00:08] James Lee: James on infra.
[00:10] Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood SE, hi all.
[00:15] Alex Morgan: cool, quick agenda, one slide, then deep into the perf numbers, tuning, and next steps. if anyone has changes shout.
[00:28] Priya Nair: okay jumping in — last week we ran the baseline with continuous batching enabled, default batch window 20ms, concurrency 8, queue depth 50. results were: sustained throughput ~ 1,900 rps for the small prompt set, median latency ~ 70ms, tail p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 680ms. KV cache hit rate roughly 42%.
[00:50] James Lee: yeah we saw that on our side too, the tail at p99 spiked during the burst window and caused some timeouts on the frontend.
[00:55] Sofia Park: that 680ms p99 is kinda high for our chat micro-interactions — we'd like p99 under 350 ideally.
[01:02] Alex Morgan: understood. tradeoffs here are bigger batches give you better throughput and lower cost, but they can increase tail latency for single requests, especially when concurrency is low and queue depth is limited.
[01:16] Priya Nair: right, a few notes — the continuous-batching window can be tuned; increasing window to 40ms increased batch sizes which improved tokens/sec but pushed p99 up slightly. Also KV cache warmup matters: during our 10-minute run the cache settled and hit-rate climbed from 30% to 52% which helped later throughput.
[01:38] Marta Ruiz: is KV "cash" — sorry I mean cache — mostly helpful for prefix-heavy chats? our usage has a lot of short-turn prompts and system messages so not sure how big the benefit will be.
[01:47] Priya Nair: yes mainly prefix reuse helps. for ephemeral per-request prompts it's less. but we found even partial reuse for system tokens helps.
[01:55] Alex Morgan: Metrics we should optimize toward: 1) median latency under 100ms, 2) p95 < 250ms, 3) p99 < 350ms, and throughput >= target (2k rps for web tier).
[02:10] Sofia Park: those are the right targets. What's the fastest config to try next?
[02:14] Priya Nair: Proposal A: keep continuous batching, bump concurrency to 12, queue depth to 100, batch window 25ms. Proposal B: reduce batch window to 10ms and raise concurrency to 16 to prioritize lower tail lat but lose some throughput efficiency.
[02:30] James Lee: can our infra sustain concurrency 16 across the GPU pool? we have reserved 4xA100 nodes for this POC.
[02:35] Priya Nair: with current model quantization (8-bit) the GPU memory looks fine for 16 concurrency but kernel saturation might increase. we'd also recommend enabling the per-shard autoscale to allow burst capacity for short spikes — set trigger at 75% GPU utilization and cool-down 30s.
[02:53] Alex Morgan: also note queueing behavior: if queue depth is too low many requests get immediate backpressure and fail; too high and you get long wait times in queue. 100 is a reasonable mid.
[03:04] Marta Ruiz: what about fallbacks to cheaper model variants during heavy load?
[03:07] Priya Nair: yes we can route to a quantized smaller variant automatically; Redwood supports model variant fallback with low-latency check and graceful degrade. caveat: eval quality may drop — we'll show a quick A/B on quality after throughput runs.
[03:22] Alex Morgan: okay action plan: we'll run three controlled 10-minute benchmarks with different configs — (1) concurrency 8 / qd 50 / window 20ms (baseline), (2) concurrency 12 / qd 100 / window 25ms (throughput-first), (3) concurrency 16 / qd 100 / window 10ms (latency-first). we'll capture p50/p95/p99, kv hits, GPU utl, tokens/sec.
[03:44] Sofia Park: sounds good. For the benchmarks please also include a synthetic burst test that simulates 400ms user think-time then 30 requests in a second, to reproduce the frontend timeouts.
[03:55] Priya Nair: good call, we'll add a burst pattern in the spreadsheet.
[04:00] Alex Morgan: quick note on autoscaling — if you prefer reserved Dedicated later, we can change autoscale policies to be more aggressive for dedicated GPU pools, but for hosted POC this config works.
[04:12] James Lee: can you share the exact commands or config keys? we tried editing the runtime json last week and hit an error.
[04:18] Priya Nair: yes I'll send a 1-pager with the runtime flags: continuous_batching.window_ms, concurrency.target, queue.max_depth, autoscale.trigger_pct, fallback.variant_priority. Also a sample curl and k8s snippet for private.
[04:31] Marta Ruiz: any security blockers if we push more load? we still need to finish SOC2 checklist and SSO setup.
[04:36] Alex Morgan: security work is separate, but noted — we can schedule a security deep-dive next week. it won't block the perf runs but for private deployment you'll need the PKI stuff.
[04:45] Sofia Park: timeline question — if the benchmarks look good, what's the path to production?
[04:49] Alex Morgan: typical path: finalize config, run a 24h soak test to validate long-tail and cache behavior, then can move to pilot ring (10% traffic) for 1 week, then full rollout. we can also set canary rollouts and auto-fallbacks.
[05:00] Priya Nair: I'll include suggested soak test parameters in the how-to.
[05:05] Alex Morgan: ok let's open for quick clarifying questions.
[05:08] James Lee: when you say queue depth 100, is that global per node or per route?
[05:12] Priya Nair: it's per route by default, can be configured per-model. for your setup it's per-service.
[05:18] Sofia Park: are there any throttles at the control plane that could affect bursts?
[05:21] Alex Morgan: control plane throttles are minimal for POC but rate limits at account level exist; we'll bump your quota for the test window.
[05:28] Marta Ruiz: can we get the redwood console link to watch metrics live?
[05:31] Alex Morgan: yes will share console link and a short video showing where to watch GPU utl, KV hits, batching heatmap.
[05:38] Priya Nair: one more point — on the model side if you enable quantization to int8 we saw a 20% throughput gain but sometimes higher variance in tail lat depending on kernel choices. we'll keep one run with quantized model.
[05:52] Sofia Park: alright makes sense. thanks.
[05:55] Alex Morgan: recap: Redwood runs 3 bench configs + burst pattern; Priya sends config how-to; Sofia confirms acceptable tail-lat by Friday; we meet next Monday. i'll share the sheet and console link after the call. any final?
[06:10] Marta Ruiz: no, thanks all.
[06:12] Alex Morgan: thanks, bye.
duration_summary: 45 minutes: rollcall (2m), perf recap (6m), tuning proposals (10m), infra Q&A (8m), action plan and next steps (5m), wrap (2m).
